newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt wants more active U.S. role in Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Egypt wants more active U.S. role in Mideast.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, in remarks published on Wednesday, urged the United States to take a more active role in reviving Middle East peace talks.
U.S. envoy Dennis Ross has been in the region on his second visit in a month trying to arrange a meeting between Israel and the Palestinians.
Asked if Ross had come with new ideas that could dispel Palestinian fears that he was biased towards Israel, Moussa answered:
"I will not go into accusations that any American official or anyone else is biased or not. Ross just represents U.S. policies and diplomacy in the Middle East peace process.

"We call for balance in this policy...I urge Amercian diplomacy, which is dynamic, to be more active and to play the role of the honest broker who works to implement the principle of land for peace," Moussa told the London-based Arabic-language daily newspaper al-Hayat.
Negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians have been largely stalled since Israel broke ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.
Moussa said Arabs were keen to emphasise to Israel their insistence on a "balanced peace".

"We want to send the real message to Israel that says: 'If you want peace we are willing but according to the bases that we agreed upon in Madrid and Oslo. We can never emphasise extremism or obstacles because we insist on the principle of land for peace," Moussa said.
"Sensible policy is based on connecting of this principle with the Madrid framework with the aim of peace that benefits both Israel and the Arabs. This is what we must insist upon.
"Egyptian policy will never agree to presenting the Palestinians on a silver platter to Israeli policy. We are trying to solve the Palestinian issue not destroy it," he added.

Egypt has become increasingly critical of Israel since right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu came to power last year and has often called on him to stick to the framework established for the peace talks during the 1991 Madrid Middle East peace conference.
